summary: Two suspicious iia values: area=2663 ha and production=2873.5 t are implausibly low; a third value of 2460450 t is implausibly high. The low values likely reflect a Chinese unit (thousand piculs/shi) mis-labeled as ha/tonnes in layer_b consolidation. The 2460450 t value is characteristic of 1930s iia data (IIA 1934-1938 averages: 2.32-2.71 Mt) and is either a temporally misassigned 1930s row or a unit-mismatch between an old iia pub (1000 quintals) and a newer pub (metric tonnes). Historical range for China groundnut production ca. 1909-1913 was likely 50k-200k t (Mitchell shows 404k t by 1922; iia export figures exceed 52k t in 1909-1913 average). Audit required: (1) trace raw source document for 2460450 t value; (2) verify unit column for 2873.5 t and 2663 ha in older iia pub; (3) flag both observations as unit-unverified and exclude from production aggregation until resolved. Polity CHN-1895-1913 itself is correct (CShapes 2.0 feature 710 vintage 1899).

summary: Confirmed data ingestion error in data/external/before_1961.csv for China mainland goats sourced from mitchell/page251-300.xlsx sheet page_41_table_1. Root cause: the import script applied a wrong unit multiplier to the raw Excel values (which are in thousands, unit column B=1000), yielding values ~1001x too large for 1950-1960 and ~2x too large for 1945-1947. Specifically: the reviewed Excel has raw values like 1821 (1950) in column J; these should be multiplied by 1000 to get heads (1821000 goats in 1950), but stored values are e.g. 1822821000 = 1821 * 1001 * 1000. For 1945-1947 the Excel goats values (13249 13609 13976) are stored as 26498000 / 27218000 / 27952000 = exactly 2000x each raw value instead of 1000x. The 1949 cell J7 is a text annotation '16130 millions'; the import parsed the numeric part 16130 and stored 16146130 which is only 0.1% above the correct ~16130000 and is plausible. No territorial or polity-boundary action needed. Action required: fix the import pipeline to apply unit multiplier x1000 only (not x1001000) for China mainland goats rows from page_41_table_1 then regenerate before_1961.csv and re-run the flag pipeline. The corrected 1950 value should be 1821000 heads (not 1.82 billion); 1950-1960 series should all be divided by 1001; 1945-1947 series should be divided by 2. Source file: /home/usuario/Nextcloud/WHEP_ERC 2025/Sources/data_raw/sources_reviewed/mitchell/Agriculture without Europe data/page251-300.xlsx sheet page_41_table_1 column J (Goats).

label: Australia Fiji
summary: Confirmed digitisation error in r_fao_crops_1952_76_77_groundnuts.xlsx. The original FAO 1952 PDF (page 77, OCEANIA section) shows two distinct rows — Australia and Fiji — which were merged into the compound label 'Australia Fiji' during manual data entry; additionally, Australia's 1949 production was recorded as 81 (instead of 8) and 1950 as 61 (instead of 6), because the digit '1' from the Fiji row immediately below was concatenated to Australia's figures. Yield cross-check confirms corrections: 8000 t / 7000 ha = 1.14 t/ha matches PDF yield 11.2 (100 kg/ha); 6000 t / 7000 ha = 0.86 t/ha matches PDF yield 8.0. No alias is emitted — the label is erroneous and must not be routed anywhere. Required actions: (1) split the merged xlsx row back into two rows; (2) fix Australia production 1949 from 81->8 and 1950 from 61->6; (3) route corrected Australia rows to AUS-1901-2025; (4) route Fiji rows to FJI-1800-2025 (Fiji has no area data, production ~1 thousand t).
